lane_impact: L5 combat-core: rewrite RR:155 as MASTERY-10, and drop RR:157's 'decide-and-flag' — the mastery curve is now fully modelled, not a choice. STANCE_DMG_MULT = {light 0.5 + 0.04m, balanced 1 + 0.02m, heavy 1.4}; STANCE_REACH_MULT = {light 1.4, balanced 1 + 0.02m, heavy max(0.5 + 0.04m, 100/base)}; MASTERY_MAX = 10. Note the ledger's reach triple is the mastery-ZERO row while its damage triple is the mastery-TEN row — they were never the same row, which is what made the tables look contradictory.
ledger_text: 3. **The stance tables (dmg 0.9/1.2/1.4, reach 300/200/100) are MASTERY-9 CEILING values, not base.**
text: RR:155 calls the stance tables 'MASTERY-9 CEILING values' and RR:157 offers 'decide-and-flag the build targets mastery-9'. Off by one, and the web source settles it exactly. DAMAGE, §1t99s0§.as:3262-3270: Light x(0.5 + 0.4 x lightMastery x 0.1) = 0.5 + 0.04m; Balanced x(1 + 0.02m); Heavy/Dual/Reversed x1.4 FLAT. At m = 10 that is exactly 0.9 / 1.2 / 1.4 — the ledger's own triple, to the digit. At m = 9 it is 0.86 / 1.18 / 1.4, which is not the triple. The reach multipliers do the same thing at :3094/:3105/:3116: at m = 10, 1.4 / 1.2 / 0.9, and RR:156's independent 'Heavy's reach also scales x0.5 -> x0.9' is exactly 0.5 + 0.04m across m = 0..10. RR:156's other half is confirmed too: at m = 0 the damage row is 0.5 / 1.0 / 1.4, precisely 'a level-1 Shugyosha does Light x0.5 / Balanced x1.0 / Heavy x1.4 (Heavy is fixed)'. So stance mastery runs 0..10 inclusive, the wiki tables are the mastery-TEN row, and 'Heavy is fixed' is true for damage and false for reach — which is why the damage and reach tables have inverted shapes. Corroborated outside the code: strings.json["8131"]-["8133"] are 'Light/Balanced/Heavy Stance Mastery Level 10.' achievements — level 10 is the terminal rung.

quote: §1t1523s0§.as:2644 'if(§1t7356s0§(§1t9426s0§) == 8)' :2646 '§1t9713s0§(§1t9413s0§,100);' :2651 '§1t9713s0§(§1t9413s0§,25);' · :228 'internal static const §1t9413s0§:int = 12;' ‖ android StatsManager.as:194 'internal static var STAT_HGOLD:int = 12;' :2203 'changeStat(STAT_HGOLD,20);' :2207 'changeStat(STAT_HGOLD,5);'
text: RR:165 justifies demoting tenthGold=100 to INFERRED with 'film shows a flat +25 gold every rebirth, no 10th-rebirth tier'. The web build's own rebirth routine contradicts the second half, four lines above the cite the dan-rank claim in this packet already used. §1t1523s0§.as:2644-2651: 'if(§1t7356s0§(§1t9426s0§) == 8) { §1t9713s0§(§1t9413s0§,100); ... } else { §1t9713s0§(§1t9413s0§,25); }'. §1t9413s0§ is const 12 at :228, and android StatsManager.as:194 gives STAT_HGOLD = 12, so this is the gold grant. Dan == 8 is the rebirth that takes the player to the tenth rung (dan is 0-based, displayed +1 at :2659), so the tenth rebirth pays 100 and every other rebirth pays 25. The +25 half of RR:165 is CONFIRMED by source; the 'no 10th-rebirth tier' half is FALSE, and tenthGold = 100 is CONTRACT on web v0.717, not INFERRED. This closes the half of RR:164-165 that the packet's dan-rank claim explicitly declined to touch, so RR:164-165 now falls whole. BUILD DIVERGENCE, stated because a recreation must choose: android StatsManager.as:2201-2207 pays 20 and 5, not 100 and 25 — the web numbers are the v0.717 target.

ledger_text: 4. **In-combat stance is HARD-LOCKED in v0.717** ("CANNOT CHANGE STANCE"). The recreation's Focus-gated in-combat switch models **removed 2014 behavior**.
text: RR:158 opens claim 4 with 'In-combat stance is HARD-LOCKED in v0.717 ("CANNOT CHANGE STANCE")', treating the on-screen caption as proof of a lock. The caption is the Focus bar's ZERO-STATE LABEL. Web BattleUI §1t113s0§.as:326-359 is updateReload: it computes _loc3_ = (reload - 48) / (maxreload - 48) clamped at 0, sets the bar scaleX to it, and then drives ONE textfield §1t5169s0§ through three states — _loc3_ == 0 shows the grey §1t5204s0§ (:111, getString(960)), 0 < _loc3_ < 1 hides it, _loc3_ >= 1 shows the black §1t5203s0§ (:110, getString(175) = 'Critical Hit') and plays Snd_criticalDamage. The -48 offset is the same 48 the stance switch costs (§1t99s0§.as:3060, :3162), so the bar reads empty and the caption shows precisely while the switch is unaffordable. I OPENED THE FRAMES AND LOOKED, in both longplays. reference/frames/duel_dense/Nr4fQstqHDM_428.0.png and reference/frames/combat_frames/Nr4fQstqHDM_t0445s.png / _t0505s.png (battle, no overworld '+' button) show HP and Chi bars above a third bar that is EMPTY, captioned 'CANNOT CHANGE STANCE'. reference/frames/combat_frames/Nr4fQstqHDM_t0170s.png / _t0530s.png and reference/frames/zFt_combat/zFtCaTO0_1M_t0320s.png (overworld, '+' button and speech bubble visible) show that same slot reading 'HEAVY STANCE' / 'BALANCED STANCE' — the OverworldHUD bust text, getString(645)/(644). Both longplays are early low-level fights, so the meter had not reached 48. THE FRAME AND THE CODE AGREE; the ledger's reading of the frame is what fails. Corroborating detail: getString(960) has no entry in the v0.682 string table (2,533 rows, ids 959/960/961 all absent) and android BattleUI.as:259-263 has no such caption and no -48 offset at all — the two-state caption is a v0.717 web addition, which is why the Android artifacts could not explain the text.

quote: InputManager.as:231 'if(mouseY > 480)' · :342 'mouseX = (stageMC.mouseX - StatsManager.stageOffsetX) / StatsManager.stageScale;' · :198 'distanceLeft = maxDistance;' · :367 'distanceLeft -= distanceTravelled;' ‖ MCSPlayer.as:3094 'InputManager.setMaxDistance(this.slashLength);'
text: One packet finding closed RR:190 blocker ① 'in STAGE PIXELS' and the other explicitly held the unit question open ('What is NOT closed: the unit-to-stage-px scale factor, which still wants one frame measurement'). The open half is closed, and not from the inventory text — from the input path that consumes the number. MCSPlayer.as:3092-3094 passes the freshly computed slashLength straight into InputManager.setMaxDistance, InputManager.as:106-108 stores it as maxDistance, and :198 loads distanceLeft = maxDistance at mouse-down. The drawn blade path then spends that budget in Euclidean units of the DESCALED stage space: :342-343 compute mouseX/mouseY as (stageMC.mouseX - StatsManager.stageOffsetX) / StatsManager.stageScale, :355 takes the squared distance between consecutive descaled points, and :367 subtracts it from distanceLeft. That coordinate space is the native game stage — :348 bounds it by StatsManager.stageWidth/stageHeight and :231 rejects any release with mouseY > 480, the literal native height. So slashLength is a length in native 800x480 stage pixels by construction, no scale factor outstanding: a 1080p capture is that space times 1080/480 = 2.25 (before pillarbox). No frame measurement is needed, and none should be commissioned.

Together with the slash-length formula this also closes the 'SPD range/cooldown scaling' half of RR:200 progression blocker ①, leaving only the DEF mitigation curve there.
quote: §1t1523s0§.as:2291-2295 'if(param1 > 600) { param1 = 600; } return 1 - param1 / 600 * 0.5;' ‖ android StatsManager.as:1854-1860 'internal static function getSkillCooldownModifierVal(speed:int) : Number { if(speed > 300) { speed = 300; } return 1 - speed / 300 * 0.5; }'
text: RR:195 skills-meters blocker ④ is bare: 'SPD->cooldown formula'. RR:90-91 lists 'the SPEED-stat->cooldown formula' as a KNOWN-UNKNOWN, and RR:200 progression blocker ① asks to measure 'SPD range/cooldown scaling ... per-point deltas in a build'. The formula is in web v0.717 source, two functions below the slash-length one. §1t1523s0§.as:2289-2296 is 'if(param1 > 600) { param1 = 600; } return 1 - param1 / 600 * 0.5;' and its caller applies the same SPD + gear-bonus + x1.5-speed-buff preamble the slash-length getter uses. Android StatsManager.as:1844-1860 names it getSkillCooldownModifier / getSkillCooldownModifierVal, confirming what the obfuscated pair is. So SKILL_COOLDOWN_MULT = 1 - min(SPD_eff, 600)/600 * 0.5, a linear ramp from 1.0 at SPD 0 to a hard floor of 0.5 at SPD 600 — skill cooldowns can be halved and no further. It is displayed to the player as '0.xxx' next to slash distance (web §1t5957s0§.as:3014 getString(983) + int(modifier * 1000); android InventoryUI.as:2233 'skill cooldown modifier: '). BUILD DIVERGENCE: android caps at 300, not 600 — 'if(speed > 300) { speed = 300; } return 1 - speed / 300 * 0.5;' — so the web ramp is half as steep and a v0.717 recreation must take 600.
